Rashi on Ketubot 62b:10:1.hebrew: איעקרא - נעשית עקרה, כן דרך העומדות עשר שנים בלא בעל:
Rashi on Ketubot 62b:10:1.english: She became infertile - She became barren; such is the way of [women] who remain ten years without a husband.

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:11:1.hebrew: בשילהי הלוליה דר' שמעון - סוף ימי חופתו:
Rashi on Ketubot 62b:11:1.english: At the end of Rabbi Shimon’s wedding feast - [At] the end of the days of his wedding.

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:11:2.english: Wait for me - Wait for me until the days of my wedding are over, and I will go with you to the study hall.

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:11:3.english: The paths of the city had changed - For new buildings were built in the city and alleyways were blocked up in it.

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:12:1.english: A certain girl - A young girl.

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:12:2.hebrew: סוי לבה - ראה לבה, כלומר נדמה ללבה פתאום שזה בעלה:
Rashi on Ketubot 62b:12:2.english: Her heart fluttered [sevi libah] - Her heart saw; that is to say, it suddenly seemed to her heart that this was her husband.

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:13:1.english: I will not do as Bar Ḥakhinai did - Who entered his house suddenly.

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:13:2.english: He sat before him - And the father did not recognize him.

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:13:3.english: She saw - [i.e., he saw] his son, that his teachings were sharp.

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:13:4.hebrew: אי הואי הכא - אילו הייתי כאן כשהנחתי בני קטן והלכתי, הייתי מלמדו תורה והיה חכם כזה:
Rashi on Ketubot 62b:13:4.english: If I had been here - If I had been here when I left my young son and went away, I would have taught him Torah and he would have been wise like this [man].

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:15:1.hebrew: כלבא שבוע - שם א' מעשירי ירושלים, שכל הנכנס לביתו רעב ככלב הי' יוצא שבע:
Rashi on Ketubot 62b:15:1.english: Kalba Savua - [The] name of one of the wealthy [men] of Jerusalem, for anyone who entered his house [as] hungry as a dog would leave satiated.

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:1:1.hebrew: אכולהו - נמי קאמר, דע"י נדר יתר משבת אחת לא:
Rashi on Ketubot 62b:1:1.english: With regard to all of them - [The tanna] also states [this], that through a vow, more than one week [is] not [permitted].

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:1:2.english: But - Without a vow, it states six months for sailors.

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:1:3.hebrew: אינו דומה - לענין תענית, מי שיש לו כו'. אף כאן, בלא נדר, דעתה נוחה לבעלה שמא יבא בתוך הזמן; אבל זו, משהדירה, הרי היא כמי שאינה מצפה לבעל:
Rashi on Ketubot 62b:1:3.english: [One] is not comparable - Regarding a fast, one who has [bread in his basket], etc. Here too, without a vow, her mind is at ease regarding her husband, [thinking] perhaps he will come within the [allotted] time; but this [woman], once he has bound her by a vow, is like one who is not expecting a husband.

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:2:1.hebrew: חמר ונעשה גמל מאי - נישאת לו כשהוא חמר, מהו ליעשות גמל שלא ברשות? הרווחה עדיפא לה שיתעשר, או עונה עדיפא לה:
Rashi on Ketubot 62b:2:1.english: [If he was] a donkey driver and became a camel driver, what [is the law] - [If] she married him when he was a donkey driver, what is [the law] as to his becoming a camel driver without [her] permission? Is financial comfort preferable to her — that he should become wealthy — or are [more frequent] conjugal relations preferable to her?

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:2:2.english: With a kav and tiflut [intimacy] - For her husband to be with her.

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:2:3.english: Than ten kavs - To become wealthy.

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:3:1.hebrew: דברי ר"א - אמתני' קאי, וסיפא דמתני' נקיט:
Rashi on Ketubot 62b:3:1.english: This is the statement of Rabbi Eliezer - [This] refers to the Mishnah, and [the Gemara] cites the end of the Mishnah.

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:3:2.hebrew: זו דברי ר"א - הנך עונות ויציאות שלא ברשות דמתני', דקתני התלמידים יוצאים לת"ת שלא ברשות שלשים יום:
Rashi on Ketubot 62b:3:2.english: This is the statement of R. Eliezer - [Referring to] those [prescribed] intervals [for marital relations] and departures without permission of the Mishnah, which teaches [that] students may leave to study Torah without permission [for] thirty days.

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:3:3.english: The Sages relied - The students in our generation rely on his words and leave without permission.

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:3:4.english: And performed an action - in accordance with him.

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:3:5.hebrew: בנפשייהו - והוא בא להם ליטול מהם נפשות, שנענשים ומתים:
Rashi on Ketubot 62b:3:5.english: With their lives - And it comes to them to take lives from them, for they are punished and die.

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:4:1.english: Mesakya [was expecting] - [This is] the Aramaic translation of metzappeh [expecting].

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:5:1.hebrew: מע"ש כו' - שהוא ליל תענוג ושביתה והנאת הגוף:
Rashi on Ketubot 62b:5:1.english: From Shabbat eve, etc. - For it is a night of delight, rest, and physical pleasure.

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:6:1.hebrew: כפו מטתו - כדת המתאבלים, דחייבין בכפיית המטה:
Rashi on Ketubot 62b:6:1.english: Turn his bed over - As [is] the law of mourners, who are obligated to overturn the bed.

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:7:1.english: He arranged [a marriage] for his son - to marry [him to] the daughter of Rabbi Chiyya.

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:7:2.english: Is there a disqualification - [Meaning] that they were not suited [to be] one couple.

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:7:3.hebrew: שפטיה בן אביטל - בן דוד היה, אביטל שם אשת דוד. ור' חייא אתי משמעי, וזהו הפסול: שר' היה מבית דוד, ולא היתה בת הבאה משמעי הוגנת לבנו, שלא היתה בת מלכים:
Rashi on Ketubot 62b:7:3.english: Shefatya ben Avital - He was a son of David; Avital [was] the name of David's wife. And Rabbi Ḥiyya was descended from Shimi, and this was the disqualification: that Rabbi [Yehuda HaNasi] was from the house of David, and a daughter descended from Shimi was not fitting for his son, as she was not a daughter of kings.

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:8:1.english: They stipulated for him twelve years - before he marries [her].

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:8:2.english: They passed her in front of him - They passed the girl in front of the groom.

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:8:3.hebrew: דעת קונך יש בך - שאמר להרחיק זמן חופתו, וחזר וקרבה מרוב חיבת כלתו:
Rashi on Ketubot 62b:8:3.english: You have your Maker's perception - For He said to delay the time of His wedding canopy, and then brought it closer out of great love for His bride.

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:9:1.hebrew: מעיקרא כתיב תביאמו ותטעמו בהר נחלתך מכון לשבתך - שיבאו לארץ, ואח"כ יבנו לו מקדש:
Rashi on Ketubot 62b:9:1.english: Initially it is written: “You bring them and plant them in the mountain of Your inheritance, the place for Your dwelling” - [Meaning] that they would enter the Land [of Israel], and afterward build a Sanctuary for Him.

Rashi on Ketubot 62b:9:2.english: And ultimately He said, "And let them make Me a Sanctuary" - in the desert.

Tosafot on Ketubot 62b:14:1.hebrew: החוט המשולש לא במהרה ינתק - לפי ששלשתן ראו זה את זה, כדאמרי' בעלמא (בב"ב נט.) שאמר ר' אושעיא דבר ואתו ושאלו לר' ביסא; לכך קרי עלייהו "החוט המשולש לא במהרה ינתק", כלומר: לא ינתק מזרעו לעולם, כדאמרי' בעלמא (ב"מ דף פה.): כיון שאדם לומד הוא ובנו ובן בנו, מכאן ואילך תורה חוזרת על אכסניא שלה, ודריש מ"ואני זאת בריתי וגו'": [וע"ע תוספות ב"ב נט. ד"ה החוט]:
Tosafot on Ketubot 62b:14:1.english: “A threefold cord is not quickly broken” - Because all three of them saw one another, as we say elsewhere (Bava Batra 59a), that Rabbi Oshaya said something and they came and asked Rabbi Bisa [about it]; therefore he applied to them [the verse], “A threefold cord is not quickly broken,” meaning: it will never be severed from his descendants, as we say elsewhere (Bava Metzia 85a): Once a person studies [Torah] — he, his son, and his son’s son — from then on the Torah returns to its lodging place, and [the Gemara there] derives [this] from [the verse], “And as for Me, this is My covenant [with them], etc.” [See also Tosafot on Bava Batra 59a, s.v. HaChut.]

Tosafot on Ketubot 62b:15:1.hebrew: דהוה צניע ומעלי - והא דאמר באלו עוברין (פסחים מט:): "אמר ר"ע: כשהייתי עם הארץ הייתי אומר: מי יתן לי תלמיד חכם ואנשכנו כחמור", משמע דלא הוה מעלי? איכא למימר, דהתם לאו משום שהיה שונא תלמידי חכמים, אלא משום שהי' סבור שמתגאין על עמי הארץ מפני תורתן, והיו תלמידי חכמים שונאים אותם; וגם משום שלא היו מניחין אותם ליגע בהם, כדאמרינן (חגיגה דף יח:): "בגדי עם הארץ מדרס לפרושים". אבל מכל מקום, שומר מצות היה. רבינו תם:
Tosafot on Ketubot 62b:15:1.english: "That he was humble and refined" - [One might ask:] Yet [from] that which it states in [chapter] Eilu Ovrin (Pesachim 49b): "Rabbi Akiva said: When I was an am ha'aretz [an unlearned person], I used to say, 'Who would give me a Torah scholar so that I could bite him like a donkey,'" it implies that he was not refined! One can say that there it was not because he hated Torah scholars, rather because he thought that they acted arrogantly toward amei ha'aretz on account of their Torah [knowledge] and that Torah scholars hated them, and also because they would not allow them to touch them, as we say (Chagigah 18b): "The garments of an am ha'aretz are [a source of] midras [impurity] for perushim [those scrupulous about ritual purity]." However, in any event, he was observant of the commandments. Rabbeinu Tam:

Tosafot on Ketubot 62b:2:1.hebrew: רוצה אשה בקב ותיפלות כו' - תימה, דאמרינן לעיל: "שאני התם דאית להו רווחא". ושמא עבודת המלך איכא רווחא טפי:
Tosafot on Ketubot 62b:2:1.english: "A woman prefers a kav with conjugal relations, etc." - [This is] astonishing, for we said above: "There it is different, because they have profit." And perhaps [in] the king's service there is more profit.

Tosafot on Ketubot 62b:2:2.hebrew: מתשעה קבין ופרישות - גרסי', דהמשרה אשתו ע"י שליש תנן (לקמן כתובות סד:) דנותן לה שני קבין ואינו פורש מתשמיש, והמורד על אשתו מתשמיש מוסיפין על כתובתה ג' דינר (לקמן כתובות סג.); ולפי חשבון ד' סאין בסלע הוי ג' דינר י"ח קבין. כן פי' בערוך:
Tosafot on Ketubot 62b:2:2.english: "Than nine kav with abstinence" - We read [the text thus], for [regarding] one who supports his wife through a third party, we learned in a Mishnah (below, Ketubot 64b) that he gives her two kav [of food] and does not abstain from marital relations, whereas [regarding] one who rebels against his wife [by abstaining] from marital relations, they add three dinar to her ketubah (below, Ketubot 63a); and according to the calculation of four se'ah per sela, three dinar equals eighteen kav. So it is explained in the Arukh.
